A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SPEED-Bench study. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching material relocated or renumbered in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark construction analyses, acceptance lengths, inference speedups, throughput measurements, and experiments on vocabulary pruning and context length.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds benchmark-selection stability analyses, tree-verification experiments, and validation of projected speedups.

M1.justification: The greedy selection and local-swap procedure, QP alternative, and measurement framework remain unchanged. Tree-based verification was already described as supported in v1; v2 supplies experiments demonstrating that capability.

E1.justification: The data sources, eleven qualitative categories, multilingual coverage, and throughput entropy categories and ISL buckets remain unchanged. The additional analyses concern subset selection, inference configurations, and speedup estimation within retained coverage.

E2.justification: Figure 2 adds selection without local-swap refinement as a comparator. SPEED(rand) becomes SPEED(uniform), representing the existing random-sampling comparator. The QP comparison and the speculative-decoding comparator set in Table 1 are retained.

E3.justification: v2 adds distinct evaluation designs: subset stability measured through relative AL ranges and ranking disagreement; tree verification sweeping top-k values 2, 4, 8 and draft lengths 3, 5, 7; and proxy validation at BS=16, DL=3, and ISLs 1k, 2k, 8k. Separately, Figure 7 narrows its reported batch-size range from 2–512 to 2–256.

E4.justification: The revision substantially expands validation of benchmark reliability and applicability. It adds the local-swap ablation, sensitivity of AL measurements and category rankings to subset selection, tree-width/depth sensitivity, and direct validation of the existing cross-domain speedup proxy. The earlier QP and systems analyses remain.

E5.justification: Appendix C.1 introduces a dedicated sampling-variability assessment, reporting ten independently constructed benchmarks per selection method, different seeds, relative AL ranges, and mean/maximum ranking disagreement. v1 lacks this repeated-selection assessment. The subsequent reference to nine optimized benchmarks leaves the exact ranking-analysis count inconsistent.

E6.justification: New results include Roleplay AL variation of 22.7% for uniform selection versus 0.6% for optimized selection, and DL=7 mean ranking disagreement of 0.056 versus 0.004. Tables 9–10 add tree-verification ALs and projected-versus-measured speedups differing by at most 0.02×. Figure 7 removes the BS=512 endpoints. Main Table 1 and the relocated QP results are unchanged.

T1.justification: The pairwise-similarity objective, QP relaxation, acceptance-length equation, and speedup derivation are retained. The added empirical range and Kendall-τ measures do not introduce a new theoretical result, proof, or revised mathematical argument.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's three contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about diverse benchmark data, unified production-engine evaluation, and data-dependent speculative-decoding performance. The added experiments support existing claims without redefining them.

C2.justification: Section 7 explicitly distinguishes normalized input-processing factors from engine-specific numerical, scheduling, and kernel behavior retained in end-to-end comparisons. Appendix C adds an interpretation of optimized selection as making domain-difficulty conclusions less dependent on the sampled benchmark.

D1.justification: Appendix A newly documents source-specific difficulty assignments and CodeContests difficulty normalization. Section 7 adds an explanation of KV-cache rollback during batched verification. These disclose existing behavior; checkpoint lists, engine versions, training configurations, and resource access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning remain unchanged. The CoSER reference receives publication, author-order, and URL updates, but identifies the same work already cited in v1.

P1.justification: There are localized revisions to Section 7, expanded appendix organization and explanations, a new conflict-of-interest disclosure, and author-name and typographical edits. Most existing prose and the main narrative structure are retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds four tables, adds the no-local-swap series and revised legend to Figure 2, and redraws Figure 7 with a reduced range and adjusted axis scale. Several figures and Algorithm 1 move with text reflow; the original QP table becomes Table 8. The overall visual format remains stable.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens the existing benchmark through direct selection-stability tests and validation of projected speedups, supplemented by tree-verification evidence and clearer difficulty-label documentation. These provide useful, focused support for retained claims. The unexplained ten-versus-nine benchmark count in Appendix C.1 limits confidence in that analysis, but the added evidence supports a modest overall improvement.
